InputError: detect_laps(method='auto') counts laps around a loop, but this environment has no loop: its track graph has no cycle, or its area has no hole to run around.
Why: on a track, a tree maze or in an open arena the animal can always come back the way it went, so no lap goes round a loop and the laps found would have direction 'unknown'.
Fix: for back-and-forth runs on a linear track or arm, use detect_trials(env, times, positions, regions=[start, end]); to segment round trips against a template, pass method='reference' with reference_lap=, which reports each round trip's direction along the track as 'increasing' or 'decreasing'.

InputError: Interval filtering excluded ALL trajectory intervals (active gate(s) max_gap=1.0, epochs, samples out of bounds or at NaN positions).
Why: no sampling interval is left to analyse; rather than return a result in which occupancy is zero in every bin, the call refuses.
Fix: check that epochs overlap `times` (same clock, seconds); check that positions use the environment's coordinates.

InputError: Invalid times/positions passed to Environment.occupancy():
- times must be strictly increasing; 12774 timestamp(s) repeat the one before, first 0.05183333333333451 at indices 1 and 2. A repeated timestamp gives one instant two samples and the interval between them no duration. To keep the first row of each timestamp, index times and every per-sample array with keep = np.unique(times, return_index=True)[1]; if the recordings restart their clocks, analyze each recording in its own call or map them to one clock.
Why: each interval [times[k], times[k+1]) is weighted by its duration, so mis-shaped, unsorted or repeated timestamps give wrong numbers.
Fix: pass times as a sorted 1-D array of numeric timestamps in seconds, without repeats, with one numeric positions row per timestamp.
